property_summary: Any non-owner caller is never an approved logger, and every log function returns false without changing that approval status when called by a non-approved logger.
For any logger address and approval status set by the owner, every log function returns true exactly when the caller is approved and the caller's approval status is unchanged by the log call.

Setting an approved logger by the owner always changes that logger's approval status to the given value, so approvedToLog(logger) equals the status parameter after the call and the returned log function result depends on the caller's own approval.

After the owner sets a logger's approval status to true, logCreated called by that logger returns true; after setting it to false, logCreated returns false, with the caller's approval status independent of the logger's status.

For any address logger, if the owner sets that logger's approval status to true then logCreated called by that logger returns true and the caller's approval status is unchanged; if the owner sets that logger's approval status to false then logCreated called by that logger returns false.

Any logging call from an address that is not an approved logger returns false and emits no event, and setApprovedLogger can only be called by the owner (the test contract itself) and makes exactly the given logger approved.

property_summary: For any logger, after the contract owner approves it, approvedToLog(logger) is true and any subsequent logging call from that logger returns true; the approval state stays true.

When the contract owner calls setApprovedLogger to approve a logger, the approval is recorded and a subsequent logging call from that same address (which must differ from the owner) is accepted and returns true, leaving the approval state unchanged.
The owner (deployer) can approve a logger and revoke it; approvedToLog reflects exactly the last status set, and the contract itself is never approved by default.
Revoking a previously approved logger (status set to false) makes approvedToLog(logger) false and a logging call from that logger returns false, while approving it makes both true.
For a non-approved caller, every logging function returns false and never reverts, and the caller's approval status is unaffected.
For an approved logger, every logging function returns true and emits the corresponding event; the caller's approval status is unchanged.
When a non-owner caller attempts to approve a logger, the transaction reverts and the logger's approval status remains unchanged.
